newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOECHST H1 97 PRE-TAX FALLS TO 2 BLN MARK.
newsitem.headline: HOECHST H1 97 PRE-TAX FALLS TO 2 BLN MARK.

text.p: German chemical giant Hoechst AG said on Wednesday pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997 fell 54 percent to two billion marks from the previous year.
However, year-earlier earnings had been boosted by income from disposals. On a comparable basis Hoechst first-half pre-tax profit rose 10 percent.
Hoechst said its operating profit was 2.3 billion marks, down 18 percent, but up seven percent on a comparable basis.
Group sales rose by seven percent to just under 28 billion marks and foreign exchange movements contributed five percentage points to the first half sales rise.
Hoechst expected to see a slight rise in full-year operating profits on a comparable basis, but that net profit in 1997 would be lower than in 1996 because of the one-off income.

"We are optimistic that operating profit for the full year will increase slightly on a comparable basis," it said. "Since the high level of extraordinary gains on the sale of companies and shareholdings in 1996 will not be incurred in 1997, net income will be lower."
"Sales will decline markedly due to spin-offs, e.g., of the specialty chemicals business to Clariant and the polypropylene business to Targor," Hoechst said.
More than half of Hoechst's 1997 operating profit growth in the first half came from the current strength of the dollar, Klaus-Juergen Schmieder, chief financial officer, said.
"Over half of the seven percent growth in operating profit on a comparable basis came from the strength of the dollar," Schmieder told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Hoechst had raised its forecast for the dollar/mark level for this year to 1.70 marks from 1.65 marks. If the dollar stayed at its current high level then Hoechst would see stronger earnings growth in 1997.
"Naturally, however, other competitive conditions could change and dampen this effect," Schmieder said, admitting that Hoechst policy in this area was "cautious".
The dollar stood at around 1.85 marks on Wednesday.
Schmieder said that because of extraordinary income from disposals last year, the group hoped to at least match the earnings growth of the first half of the year.
"If we can maintain the operating earnings growth of seven percent seen in the first half of the year, then we would be very happy," Schmieder said.
He said volumes on a comparable basis would grow by around two percent, while growth in prices was mixed as certain areas, such as polyester, were under pressure, while others were improving.
